about: T3 workarounds of the workflow (PLAN M-decision 35). Every T3 upgrade runs `node <plugin>/bin/t3-workarounds.mjs check`; the code of each workaround carries the marker `T3-WORKAROUND(<id>)`.

workarounds.title: After /clear T3 keeps resuming the session it opened first; the hook links <cursor>.jsonl to the new session's transcript
depends_on: provider log <t3-home>/logs/provider/events.<thread, ':' -> '-'>.log with lines `[<ISO time>] ..."type":"query.open","options":{..."resume":"<session id>"`
T3 resumes the session id it opened with (claudeAgent resume cursor)
T3 sets T3CODE_THREAD_ID in the agent's environment
Claude Code appends to <session>.jsonl in place (Windows without Developer Mode: hard link instead of symlink, made by a detached process once the new transcript exists)
workarounds.pilot: pilot thread: say a code word, /clear, ask for a second word, restart the query (interrupt or T3 restart); the thread must answer from the session after /clear
workarounds.remove_when: fix PR merged and contained in the installed T3 version; then remove the marked code and this entry

workarounds.title: T3 does not show hook systemMessage; the agent prints the status block in its first reply (P-050)
workarounds.pilot: new pilot thread: does T3 show the SessionStart systemMessage? if yes, the agent-printed block is shown twice and can be dropped

workarounds.title: The hook cannot rename a thread; it reads the title via the T3 CLI and asks the agent to rename (P-036); topics start threads via the CLI
depends_on: `t3 thread start --json` prints the new thread's id
workarounds.pilot: pilot: `topic create` from a thread holding a topic opens a new T3 thread titled by the topic
workarounds.remove_when: hooks can rename threads (no CLI dependency)
